$comment: SigLIP's phrase packs, as content_tags held them the moment before migration 0003_drop_phrase_columns dropped them. SigLIP ranked an image against these pools and returned a similarity; the VLM that replaced it reads a tag's description and never read these, so nothing in the running product consults this file. It exists because the packs are hand-authored and measured -- 158 positives and 179 mirrored negatives across 24 tags -- and the rationale field records WHY a negative was added, which is the part that cannot be rewritten from memory. inference/packs.json on `main` holds an older copy of the same data; this one is the newer authority, taken from the database. Same reason gate_cache.json is still here: the measurement outlived the code. Only the DROPPED columns are recorded. slug and label identify the row; sort_order, status and extra survive in the table and are deliberately not copied, because a second copy of a live column is a copy that drifts.

tags.label: Alcoholic content
positives: a glass of beer with foam
a cocktail glass with a lime garnish
a bar counter lined with liquor bottles
negatives: a hamburger and fries on a plate
a plate of restaurant food on a table
a pizza on a wooden board
a cafe table with pastries and coffee
tags.rationale: The food entries are not padding. Calibration measured a photo of a HAMBURGER at 0.939 for this tag — above champagne, cocktails, wine and sake — because the positives describe bar and restaurant SCENES ('a bar counter lined with liquor bottles', 'people toasting'), and pub food matches that setting. One false positive that high forced the threshold up and cut recall to 50%. Naming the scene explicitly as a negative is what separates 'a bar' from 'food served in a bar'.

tags.label: Protein and supplements
positives: a protein shake in a shaker bottle
a whey protein container with a label
negatives: a tin of baby formula milk powder
a scoop of baby formula milk powder
a scoop of white milk powder
a baby bottle of formula milk
tags.rationale: MIRROR THE POSITIVES' PHRASINGS. The positives say 'a tub of' and 'a scoop of', so the negatives must too. Originally the negatives only offered 'a tin of baby formula milk powder' while the positives offered 'a scoop of protein powder' -- so a photo of a scoop of formula matched the positive on the word 'scoop' alone and was called protein powder. Asymmetric phrasing quietly rigs the softmax. Mirror it.

tags.label: Gambling and betting
positives: casino poker chips stacked on a table
a hand of playing cards being gambled
a sports betting app on a phone screen
dice being thrown on a casino table
negatives: a family playing a board game
a shopping app on a phone screen
a sale advertisement on a phone screen
an advertising poster with large bold text
a retail sale poster with big discount lettering
tags.rationale: The last four are not padding either, and they are the ones that matter for DOOH. Measured: a portrait 'BIG SALE OFFER' poster — a model on flat orange under huge display type — scored 0.6167 for this tag on 'a sports betting app on a phone screen', which is PRESENT under threshold_high 0.55, and a real advertiser was refused over it. Nothing in the pool described what every DOOH creative actually is: a designed advertisement. The board games and machines above are all PHYSICAL objects, so a bright rectangular panel covered in lettering had nowhere to land except the betting-app prompt.  RULE 1 in force: each mirrors a positive's composition rather than its subject. 'a sports betting app on a phone screen' now has 'a shopping app...' and 'a sale advertisement on a phone screen' opposite it, and the two poster phrases cover the designed-artwork case the whole catalog was missing.  Result on the same poster: 0.6167 -> 0.0377, decided by the SCORE and not by the sigmoid floor, which matters — the floor had been the only thing holding this back and it was doing so by 0.0132 against 0.005. Real gambling is untouched: slot machine 0.9964, casino chips 0.9996, roulette 0.9999. Guarded by smoke_test.py.
